sulfate-reducing prokaryotes can grow in oxic-anoxi gradients and that they are chemotactic towards their preferred electron donor, lactate, and away from the toxic compound oxygen.

the sulfate-reduducers studied here can survive exposure to air for at least 8 hours, can grow in oxygen-sulfate counter gradients in the anoxic part of the gradient and respond chemotactically towards oxygen, lactate, nitrite, nitrate, sulfite and thiosulfite.
sulfate-reducing and other anaerobes can survive and even thrive in oxic environments by reducing oxygen and that they actively change the oxygen concentration to their advantage.

the growth and chemosensitivities of sulfate-reducting bacteria in oxygen-sulphide gradients.
the chemotactic response of sulfate-reducting bacteria in oxygen-sulphide gradients.
the growth of sulfate-reduducers in oxic-anarobic interfaces and their chemotactic response to environmental factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

sulfate reducers are able to use a variety of substrates as electron donors for oxygen reduction, and that this ability may be important for the survival and growth of these microorganisms in oxic-anobic environments.
chemotaxis in sulfate-reducing prokaryotes is not a general feature but that it depends on the species and the environmental conditions.
sulfate reducers are chemotactically attracted to lactate and other electron donors, and repelled by oxygen and other oxidants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sulfate-reducing prokaryotes are able to grow in oxygen-sulfidic gradients, but they avoid high oxygen concentrations and sulfide.
the sulfate-reduducers can grow in oxic-anoxie gradients, but they preferentially grow in the anoxic part of the gradients, and they can actively change the extension of the oxic-anoxice gradient.
chemotaxis in sulfate-reducing and other anaerobic bacteria can be considered a strategy to re-establish the conditions required for anaerobic growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sulfate-reducing bacterial cells are able to survive and grow in oxygen-sulfur dioxide gradients.
sulfate-reducing prokaryotes can survive exposure to oxygen and even use it as a terminal electron acceptor.
the sulfate-reduducers are not just passive organisms in oxic-anarobic environments, but are actively involved in the creation of anoxic microsites.
